newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. calls for Afghan ceasefire, negotiations.
newsitem.headline: U.N. calls for Afghan ceasefire, negotiations.

text.p: U.N. Security Council members called on Wednesday for an immediate end to the fighting in Afghanistan and for peace negotiations.

The appeal, announced after a meeting of the Security Council by its current president, Alfredo Lopes Cabral of Guinea-Bissau, came amid reports of heavy fighting in Kabul between government forces and the radical Taleban militia.
Cabral said the 15-nation Security Council was particularly concerned by the humanitarian crisis and the risk of civilian casualties in the fighting for Kabul.
"The members of the council call upon the parties to stop fighting immediately, to agree to a ceasefire and to enter into serious negotiations," he said.

The Afghan government, which asked the Security Council to meet on the crisis, has denied that the capital is about to fall to the radical Islamic Taleban. It says it has inflicted heavy casualties on the attackers.
